steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: High Inquisitor!

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Stand down. You're no adversary for her.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: But I...

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Stand down.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: By your order!

a.text: Ten meters separate Skadi from the person before her, as they stare face to face.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You. You're very strong.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: You should not have set foot in this city.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm already here.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Violate the rules, and you must pay the price.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I can't care about that much.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: You will remain here.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't want to fight with you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Hmph. Wicked Ægir, you're surely frightened! Now that the High Inquisitor is here, you absolutely cannot run.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But, if this is necessary—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Ægirian) I will take you down.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Such speed! So much faster than her prior hand-to-hand bout with me!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: With speed like that, I could hardly even hope to touch her hemline... Just how much more was she still hiding?!

a.text: Before she collides with the High Inquisitor, Skadi steps back.
As if a fish tossed in the air by the ocean waves, she leaps high, and lands on a dilapidated roof.

The High Inquisitor follows in mirror fashion. Their figures crash together, pull apart, then crash again. The city can barely endure such a clash, torn apart as it is, and fragments of buildings are building up rapidly on the street.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Her attack and evasion are becoming more and more rapid, as are my instructor's. I almost can't keep up now.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Was I really... still this lacking?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: No, this won't do. That's an Ægir. Of course I cannot lose to an Ægir.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Yet this Ægir seems, somehow, to be using that case of hers as a weapon... Just what is that made of?! Why is it so tough?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: But my instructor isn't using the handcannon. If he was... wouldn't we have her seized in a blink? It'd blow this entire street into slag.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Is that... simply an Ægir, however? Her appearance is nothing at all like those monsters...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: She's using... some form of Arts, is it? I can't quite tell. And our lamp... cannot inhibit her power whatsoever.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: —This Ægir has too many secrets kept with her.

a.text: The shaking throughout the whole street gradually ceases. Amidst the shards and smoke, the senior Inquisitor appears again.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: High Inquisitor! You're victorious. I knew no one could ever sway you by even a hair.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Er, where's that Ægir?

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Fled.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What? That... how?

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: She is injured, and cannot run far.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I'll search for her—

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: You cannot overcome her.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Ahem... But we absolutely cannot allow her sort to run free along the coast!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Direction suggests she may have made for the citizens' assembly area. She's likely mixed in with the crowd, and has accomplices among the citizens aiding her. I'll search the houses for her one by one.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: If you believe this is right, then go.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Understood—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: High Inquisitor, was she the one who brought anomaly upon this city?

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: I had you go and see. What was it you saw?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The behavior of the locals is highly abnormal. It's as if they live every day in an unwoken state. They act, yet not to complete anything. When they eat, it's not even to fill their stomachs.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They're entering the sea, and they don't even consider it suicide.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Did you put a stop to them?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Yes. This is evidently wrong, after all.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: What we are concerned with is the results. If you believe your corrections can have right results, then go do so.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Right results...

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: If they cannot, then you must make some choices.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Inquisitor—with your own two eyes, your blade, you must stare down the greatest menaces to Iberia.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The greatest menace to Iberia... is those monsters presently climbing ashore.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Could it be? These people who head into the ocean have some relation to these monsters?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Yes... they are surely related.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I remember you once taught that abnormality often takes more than a single form. Between all these terrible visions, there must be connections.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: To address an issue—you must first see clearly where that issue lies.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I—I know!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: —It's those Ægirs hidden in the darkness, conspiring everything!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They're hidden ashore, concealed in the minor loopholes of our laws, rotting our cities' skin and flesh, destabilizing our fellows' wills, attempting to corrode our country's muscle and bone.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Before their plot prevails, before it drags this city into the abyss of despair—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: We must—find them—and wipe them out!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer... singer? Are you in here?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I've been searching for you forever. The Inquisitors won't know about this place. There are too many empty houses here, and come night, searching will be awfully hard.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I know... I'm sure you want to avoid us. That the farther you stay from where we live, the better.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Finding you here definitely wasn't easy... phew... it's so close to the coast.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Is this the sound of the waves? I never knew it was so loud. And... I can hear breathing now.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, what are you doing in here? Your breathing's become quite different.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're all in danger.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What are you talking a... um, what's—are you hurt?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm bleeding. Get away!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Thinking of leaving? It won't be that easy.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: The Inquisitor?! Did you follow me the whole way...? I—I didn't realize.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I could hardly let a commoner notice me. *cough* Of course, even if I don't tail you, I'd still have methods of finding this place!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You again.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What's wrong? Scared now?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Earlier—Ahem—I concede, I was negligent for a moment, and narrowly let you escape.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: But now, Ægir, I'll definitely have you caught!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: B—But, she's already hurt—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Hmm? Are you certain about getting in my way, so as to protect a dangerous Ægir, citizen? If so, you'll become a criminal, the same as her!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You and all the others are unalike. At the very least, your eyes show fear.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Until now, you have not yet done wrong. Out of the way! I don't want to have to sort you out with my blade.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's not the time—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: It's not what time? Are... Are you scorning me? You think I have absolutely no way to seize you?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Hmph. Certainly, I may not be the High Inquisitor. But I've already made my preparations.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I will deal with you, no matter the cost to me!

a.text: Sword still unsheathed, Skadi proceeds to grasp the Inquisitor's arm—pulling her behind Skadi's own self.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What—What is the meaning of this?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't make noise.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Unhand me, you Ægir reprobate! You'd better not think I can't employ my sword with a hand pinned, and I still have the handcannon—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Keep it down. They'll hear you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Ngh-ghhh... I can't move... my other hand either...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Um, can either of you hear something?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I heard... sticky things, rubbing along the floor... so, so many... and the sound was right outside.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What... is that? It's not the work of any of us. I've never heard it before...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They're closing in.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Their numbers are growing.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: What is causing it? The people of this place, or that woman and her companion?

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Ten of them—

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Twenty of them.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: —Still growing, still advancing. Something is leading them to clamber ashore, and spill into the city.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: And their course stems from—

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: The chapel.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Hm? They are very excited.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Are you sure you should be petting these things so?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Pay mind to the words you use. They are not 'things' of any sort. They are already a part of this expanse of ocean. They have become the heirs born of the sea, and are much purer than you are.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Ah... the news on the tide has already arrived. Tonight will be yet another special one.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: They have surely smelt the scent. When bloodkin join them, they become so spirited, so agitated, that they even wish to emerge from the sea, and give their welcome on land.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: It is very normal. We all love our own brothers and sisters.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Do you truly treat them as your own brothers?

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Why not, I ask? At times of necessity, I am willing to address those of land, those who cannot help but still walk on two legs, as my brothers too.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: If you did not hold the most dirtied, mixed blood within you, then one day, you may also possess this chance.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Oh? What a crying shame.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: (He touches the seawater.)

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Fascinating. This evening... they seem to be especially vigorous. Perhaps because so many old friends have come as guests to their home.

steps.name: Bishop
steps.text: Are you not curious? Wondering just what is happening upon the surface.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: ...Loud.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: So loud. I cannot sleep.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: Stuff your head in your quilt.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: I cannot hear.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: I cannot see.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Ngh... So hungry...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: So hungry.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: So hungry.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Ah!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Uwargh-wah-hh—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They're here.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What—What are these horrendous things?! Black... flowers? Or fish? Why do they move? How disgusting, eugh...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: It couldn't be... That's not right, this doesn't make sense!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: They're knocking on the windows! Are they... do they want to enter?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: W—We cannot let them!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Close the windows shut—

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's pointless. The windows here are all broken. Look at the top, it's full of cracks...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: —They're reaching in!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Uwargh, it's still moving! Is this tiny chunk writhing on the floor trying to force its way to us?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Even supposing it's one of those things... nothing gives it the right to be so difficult!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: So very many... there's still so many outside.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Why can I not cut them down?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: My lamp... no, the lamp would be of no use against them.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I only have enough ammunition for one more round.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I—Inquisitor?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Freeze! In a moment, I'll fire, and you two run for the interior. The ruins ought to be a little sturdier than these worn-out windows.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Your hand is trembling...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Holy scriptures... lend me strength.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I—I do not fear them!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I'll head out right away, kill as many as I can, and I should be able to hold a wave back. You must run with haste...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You, take her and hide inside.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What? What are you spouting?! Have you not seen? I can't cope with—this many! They're nigh coming in already. There's no difference between the inside and outside!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Remember, as far from doors and windows as possible.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You utterly don't listen to people when they tell you—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll go out. Draw them away.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, you can't go outside either...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You're very strong, stronger than anyone I've seen before, but you're hurt! And these odd things—there's—there's so many of them!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Inquisitor, don't—don't leave either...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What if we all hide together? I—I know there's a cupboard in here, and the door still closes. It's in the back. If all three of us squeeze, we should hopefully...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I have to go out. Only this way, will you survive.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Hey! Ægir, even if you want to play the hero, this isn't your place to!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Listen well. This is genuinely nothing to do with you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Because—they're here looking for me.
Skadi pushes open the door.
A long-lost scent following the sea breeze bores into the brain's tissue, creatures never of dry land pack densely into the streets.
They bubble up and down, spitting, contracting, imitating rot and growth in their actions, the shore of civilization falling to their sinister bodies.
